name: FDA approval explained
scope: All drug products marketed in U.S. interstate commerce
direct_answer: A drug must have an FDA-approved application in effect before it can be legally introduced into interstate commerce, unless a specific exemption applies. Approval is granted to a specific product, indication, route, strength, and dosage form.

definitions.definition: New Drug Application under section 505(b) of the FD&C Act.
Abbreviated New Drug Application for generic copies of approved drugs.
The molecule responsible for a drug's effect; not the same as an approved finished drug product.

decision_logic: 1. Is there an FDA-approved NDA/ANDA/BLA in effect for the exact product? 2. If yes, what indication, route, and strengths are approved? 3. If no, is there a lawful exemption (e.g., compounding, investigational, shortage)? 4. Do not infer approval from an advisory committee vote, a docket, a nomination, or a shortage.
examples: Tirzepatide is an active ingredient; Mounjaro and Zepbound are FDA-approved products containing it.
BPC-157 is not an approved drug even though it is sold online as a 'peptide' or dietary supplement.
limitations: This page does not cover devices, cosmetics, or foods.
It does not provide legal advice for a specific product shipment or prescription.
